findings.statement: CD70 is a surface protein with a high ADC suitability score, ranking among the top few of about two thousand candidates, which is consistent with it being a known conjugate target. [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746] No Human Protein Atlas staining data were available for it, and the CSPA surface observation is only putative, so off-tumour safety rests on the GTEx proteome, where it is not enriched in any vital organ.

CA9 is a known target with strong tumour increase, but its vital-organ protein tissue-specificity is high in stomach (a safety concern for an ADC or radioligand), and the Human Protein Atlas shows high staining there with none in kidney. [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; vital_organ_protein_ts_max=5.19] A high score does not show a conjugate would work.

SCARB1 is the top-ranked target in the convergence ranking and is observed at the cell surface (CSPA high confidence), but it is enriched in adrenal gland in the GTEx proteome, stains highly in vital organs and moderately in kidney, and only a small share of tumour cells express it in the weakest quarter of donors. [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%] This makes it a poorer conjugate candidate than its rank suggests.

SLC16A3 scores well as a conjugate target, with the most homogeneous tumour expression of the genes I checked. [gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=43.7%] It is a twelve-segment transporter with few extracellular residues, was not observed at the surface in CSPA, and stains highly in adrenal gland, so antibody accessibility is a real doubt.

Higher CD70 expression is associated with longer benefit on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab. [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=-0.383] The adjusted p-value is not significant, the combination arm does not differ from sunitinib, and the CheckMate nivolumab trial shows no difference between nivolumab and everolimus, so this is only a lead.

CA9 expression is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib. [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336] None of the arms reaches significance after correction and the combination-versus-sunitinib difference is not significant, so CA9 is not a treatment-selection marker on this evidence.

PSAT1 (lower in tumours than normal tissue) is associated with earlier progression with higher expression in every arm tested, including both arms of the CheckMate nivolumab-versus-everolimus trial and atezolizumab, but no adjusted p-value is close to significance and nivolumab does not differ from everolimus. It is a prognostic-direction lead at most, not a predictor of treatment effect.

EPAS1 expression is associated with longer benefit on everolimus in the CheckMate nivolumab-versus-everolimus trial. [gene=EPAS1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.everolimus_checkmate025.log_hr_per_sd=-0.183] The adjusted p-value is far from significant and nivolumab does not differ from everolimus; the small Choueiri cohort gives direction only.

CA9 is flagged as a subgroup target candidate for PBRM1 mutation, being higher in mutants in CPTAC RNA, CPTAC protein and TCGA RNA. [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148] The CPTAC protein difference is small and not significant on its own, and CA9 is lower in ccB than ccA, so the subgroup effect is modest.

PSAT1 is higher in BAP1-mutant tumours at RNA level in TCGA. [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711] The CPTAC protein difference is small and not significant, so it is not flagged as a subgroup target candidate; it is also strongly higher in ccB than ccA, consistent with a poor-prognosis subtype marker.

SCARB1 is modestly higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours in CPTAC RNA and TCGA RNA but not significant at protein level, and lower in BAP1-mutant tumours in TCGA RNA. It is not flagged as a subgroup target candidate for any gene, so it is a pan-tumour rather than subgroup candidate.

PCK1 is much lower in ccB than ccA tumours at RNA level in both CPTAC and TCGA, but the CPTAC protein difference is flat. It is not a mutation-defined subgroup target candidate, and it is lost in tumours, so it is a biomarker rather than a target.

Most CD70 tumour transcripts are attributed to immune cells in the CPTAC deconvolution. [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654] It correlates positively with CD8 and regulatory T cells, so its tumour signal partly reflects infiltration, and the treatment association with the combination is also a lead only.

About half of SCARB1 tumour transcripts come from immune cells, and it correlates negatively with the xCell immune score and with CD8 T cells. It ranks far down the immune-target list, so it is a tumour-and-myeloid gene rather than an immune-checkpoint-like target.

NNMT is assigned to tumour cells in both single-cell datasets, with the tumour share very high in Li 2022. [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.97] Zhang 2021 has only a few paired donors, so the tumour-versus-tubule fold change rests on a small sample.

The cell attribution of SLC16A3 does not hold between datasets: T and NK cells dominate in Li 2022 but tumour cells dominate in Zhang 2021, although the tumour-versus-tubule fold change is high in both. Tumour-cell specificity is therefore unresolved.

CD70 is dominated by T and NK cells in Li 2022 but by tumour cells in Zhang 2021, so the cell-type call is not replicated; this fits the high immune share seen in bulk tumour data. Whether tumour cells carry enough CD70 for a conjugate cannot be settled from these data.

SCARB1 protein rises in tumours in the confirmatory DIA cohort in the same direction as the discovery TMT data. [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334] The tool reports that it replicates, with significance in tumour-normal pairs.

NNMT protein replicates in the confirmatory cohort with a larger fold change, which should not be compared in size with the discovery TMT value because the technology differs. [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776]

PSAT1 protein is lower in tumours in the confirmatory cohort, matching the discovery direction. [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946] The one phosphosite measured in both cohorts was significant in discovery but did not replicate.

CD70 was not tested in the confirmatory cohort because it is absent or too sparse there (fewer than ten matched tumour-normal pairs). This is a coverage gap, not a failure to replicate, so CD70 protein evidence rests on the discovery data alone.

PCK1 protein is lower in tumours in the confirmatory cohort, and both phosphosites measured in the two cohorts replicate. It is a lost-in-tumour biomarker with protein support in two independent cohorts.

caveats: No gene differs between arms in IMmotion150 or between nivolumab and everolimus in CheckMate 025 after correction; all treatment results are leads (associated with, not predicts), and the Choueiri 2016 cohort has only 16 patients.
A high ADC score does not show a conjugate would work; staining data were missing for CD70, and CSPA surface observation is absent or only putative for CA9, CD70 and SLC16A3.
SCARB1 and CA9 are enriched in vital organs in the GTEx proteome (adrenal and stomach), a safety concern; the GTEx proteome has no kidney.
PSAT1, PCK1 and the other top biomarker-profile genes are lower in tumours, so they are biomarkers, not antibody targets; their treatment hazard ratios are from small arms.
Cell attribution differs between Li 2022 and Zhang 2021 for CD70, SLC16A3 and SCARB1; Zhang 2021 has few paired donors.

ENPP3, EPAS1 (beyond treatment), NNMT (ADC, treatment, subtype) and SLC16A3 (treatment, subtype) were not fully profiled across all layers within the tool-call budget; ENPP3 is a known target with high kidney staining in the Human Protein Atlas (EV:adc_profile:d5aee88146ed).
Subtype differences for immune genes can reflect infiltration rather than tumour-cell biology.
